turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one minute, this screen has frozen again. Okay, tell me, what happened?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing much, doctor. The big toe is paining a little since last night. I told her not to make a big scene.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Please doctor, he did not sleep. He was almost crying with the pain, but he will always say it is a small thing only.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which toe? Say it again, I was looking at the screen.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Right foot, the big one. It started yesterday morning... no, no, last night only, around midnight.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swelling? Redness?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): A little swelling is there. Some redness also, very mild.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It is puffed up and properly red, doctor. He could not get the slipper on.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The slipper was tight, that is all. I am managing.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you able to walk?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I am walking only, slowly. It is bearable.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): From the auto to this chair he was hopping. He is not walking fine.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you injure it? Stub the toe, kick something?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No injury. I did not hit anything.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, chills, feeling hot?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I am not hot. Otherwise I am first class.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last night his forehead was warm, doctor. I touched it myself. He was hot.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Let me open the old file, the system is crawling. When did the pain start, once more?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night, midnight. Alright, it was paining badly, throbbing, I could not sleep. If I touch it, worse. If I keep the foot still, a little better.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Same problem any time before?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Same toe, a year back. It settled itself, so I left it.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was not one year. It was about three months back, just before Holi. I had to loosen his slipper that week.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): So we have one year from you and three months from her. I will not lock a date today.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Whatever, same nonsense. They did a blood test, uric acid, and they said it was borderline. Nothing alarming, they told me.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline. Did they give you an actual number?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No number. Just borderline, that is all I was told.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): They also gave a small yellow tablet for the uric acid. He hardly took it.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I took it for two weeks... no, I stopped after four days. I don't remember the name. Yellow tablet, for uric acid only.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you on now? Any BP tablet, any sugar tablet?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the water tablet, morning time, for my BP. I take it daily. No sugar problem.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which water tablet? The name, please say it again, I clicked the wrong place.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I have the strip here. Hydrochlorothiazide. Twelve point five... no, sorry, it is twenty five milligrams. One tablet in the morning.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): And he actually takes it every day?
[SEG0034] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Not really, doctor. Two or three mornings a week he forgets, then he tells me he took it.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it. Once in a while I forget, it is nothing.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines? Penicillin, any painkiller?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies. Nothing at all.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Brufen, doctor. Some years ago he got red patches, a rash on the chest, after Brufen. I have not given it since.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): That was itching for one hour, not a rash, not an allergy. I keep telling her.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will mark that as not settled between you. Any loose motions, vomiting, burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no. Motions are normal, no vomiting, urine is fine. Appetite also normal.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): The file mentions beer. How much are you drinking these days?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends only, and very little. One beer... well, actually, Saturday and Sunday I take four or five Kingfishers. Weekdays I don't touch it.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That part is true. Weekends he finishes four or five bottles. I keep the rest locked.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Foot up on the stool, let me see. The right big toe joint is quite swollen, red, and sharply tender. Skin is intact, I don't see a cut or any pus.

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are not warm to touch just now. Triage has typed the vitals, if I read the right line... one thirty two over eighty... no, it is one thirty six over eighty four, and pulse seventy eight.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): There, no fever. I told you both.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): About the injury, you were very sure you did not knock it?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): I was sure. Well, actually, yesterday evening I kicked the chair leg and the toe hit it. I thought it was nothing, so I said no.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes, he shouted at the chair. I heard it from the kitchen.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. My working impression is an acute gout flare, with the beer, the water tablet, and a similar episode before. The knock may have set it off. I cannot fully rule out a small infection in the joint, so that stays on the list, but gout is what I am treating for.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Even so, we treat it. I will start colchicine, zero point five milligrams three times a day... sorry, not three times, twice a day, for five days. If loose motions start, stop it.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not give naproxen or any painkiller of that family today, with the Brufen question open. If that history turns out harmless and colchicine does not suit you, we might use naproxen five hundred milligrams twice a day with food. Not today.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): I already ate two Crocin last night. Enough, no? Gout tablet and all, too much fuss.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Crocin is fine, it is paracetamol. Take one thousand... no, five hundred milligrams, up to four times in a day, if the pain is still there. Not more than that.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): I also want a serum uric acid blood test today. In an attack the level can look normal, so we will not over-read it. Come back in one week with the report. If the redness is spreading or the pain is much worse, come sooner, don't sit at home.
[SEG0057] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will bring him. Should I put ice, and keep the foot up?

[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, ice in a cloth for ten, fifteen minutes at a time, foot kept up. No beer this week. Do not stop the water tablet on your own. Reception will book the blood test and the one-week visit. Sorry, I have a call waiting.

spec.situation: Man with a very painful swollen big toe since last night; drinks beer at weekends, takes a water tablet; had the same 'a year back'; says no injury then recalls kicking a chair; colchicine or NSAID plan; blood uric acid test.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
